title: Minimum Number of People to Teach
summary: Given a social network with m users and n languages numbered 1 through n, where each user knows a subset of these languages and there are friendships between some users, determine the minimum number of users to teach a specific language so that all friends can communicate.
statement: Given a social network with m users and n languages numbered 1 through n, where each user knows a subset of these languages and there are friendships between some users, determine the minimum number of users to teach a specific language so that all friends can communicate. The network does not guarantee transitive friendships.
constraints: People are one-indexed; languages[i] lists the languages person i+1 knows.
Choose one language and teach it to the fewest people so every friendship has a shared language.
hints: People outside failing friendships never need teaching.
Collect both endpoints of every friendship with disjoint language sets, then try each language.
For a candidate language, count collected people who do not know it; return the minimum.
Teaching that set repairs every failing edge, and any valid single-language plan must teach each collected non-speaker.
editorial: Teaching that set repairs every failing edge, and any valid single-language plan must teach each collected non-speaker.

tests.explanation: Only people one and two in the failing friendship need consideration; teaching either one person suffices.
Teaching language three to people one and three repairs all failing friendships, requiring two people.
